newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Doctors to discuss date for Yeltsin surgery.
newsitem.headline: Doctors to discuss date for Yeltsin surgery.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin's doctors are expected to meet on Monday to decide whether he is ready for a multiple bypass heart operation.

Pioneering U.S. heart surgery expert Michael DeBakey, who returned to Moscow on Sunday to attend the meeting and act as a consultant during the operation, says the surgery is likely to go ahead early this week.
The Russian surgeons who will carry out the operation have said little about their plans and may not announce in advance when the 65-year-old president is to go under the knife.

A Kremlin spokesman said last week the doctors could decide when to operate "any day" but indicated that the first sign the operation is imminent would be an announcement that Yeltsin has temporarily handed power to Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
Chernomyrdin has gradually taken on some of Yeltsin's duties in the four months since the president fell ill just before he was re-elected on July 3.

The Kremlin has made clear that Yeltsin will sign a decree handing over full power to his understudy, giving him control of Russia's nuclear arsenal, only just before the surgery. A second decree will annul it hours later if all goes according to plan.
Yeltsin's wife Naina says her husband is optimistic and cracking jokes at the Barvikha sanatorium just outside Moscow where doctors have been giving him health tests.
"Of course he is worried, but he is outwardly calm. He has a good contact with his doctors. I hear humour and jokes," she said in a television interview.

Russian surgeon Renat Akchurin will lead the operation, which is expected to last six to eight hours. He and DeBakey said after the last full meeting of doctors on September 25 that the operation would be in the following six to 10 weeks.
Yeltsin is regarded by Western leaders as the main guarantor of stability in Moscow five years after the Soviet Union and communist rule collapsed.
The president, who has had at least two heart attacks, has been waiting since early September while doctors have treated him for anaemia, a thyroid problem and other ailments.
The surgery is needed to improve the supply of blood to his heart. DeBakey has said he can resume normal within two months work if the operation is successful.

Russian officials have been trying to project an atmosphere of business as usual since then, despite media reports of a power struggle intensifying in the Kremlin while Yeltsin has been preparing for surgery.

Yeltsin tried to halt the infighting by sacking ambitious security chief Alexnader Lebed last month, but fears have grown that a peace deal which Lebed signed in rebel Chechnya on Aigust 31 could fall apart.
Businessman Boris Berezovsky, named last Tuesday as deputy secretary of the Kremlin's Security Council, met separatist leaders on Sunday in his first trip to Chehcnya in his new role.
His talks were intended to set up talks between the separatists and Chernomyrdin, who says he is ready to visit Chechnya to help the peace process. Details were not available.
